open_obligations: Note that Bai et al. supervise offline responses, not real-time exploratory actions.
Check whether AI feedback could judge which actions are genuinely risky, the key challenge Amodei et al. name.
Check Bai et al.'s own warning that less human feedback makes untested deployment easier.
out.other_title: Human checking of risky exploration runs into the scalable oversight problem
out.rationale: Amodei et al. note human checking of risky actions runs into scalable oversight because there are too many actions or they come too fast. Bai et al. define 'scaling supervision' as using AI to help humans supervise AI with a smaller quantity of higher-quality human supervision, and implement it by replacing human harmlessness labels with AI labels; the setting is labelling assistant responses, not checking exploratory actions of an RL agent online.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether AI assistance can reduce the amount of human oversight needed when too many decisions need checking

text: The authors use the term 'Scaling Supervision' for techniques that leverage AI to help humans supervise AI more efficiently, so that systems can be trained to behave in desirable ways (e.g. helpful, honest, harmless) with a smaller quantity of higher-quality human supervision.
title: Scaling supervision: using AI to help humans supervise AI more efficiently
